_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — DO NOT FILL WITH SAMPLE DATA. Populate verbatim from PDF.

generic_skills: Predicting outcomes and making reasoned decisions
Working with others to generate ideas
Looking for patterns and making generalisation
Talking confidently and explaining ideas/opinions clearly
Using a range of media to communicate ideas
Using mathematics to justify and support decisions
Using technology to create, manipulate and process information
Using technology to collaborate, communicate and refine work
Respectfully responding to people of all cultures
Appreciating ethnicity as a cradle for creativity and innovation
values: Honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness, and sound character

themes.theme_description: Learners are expected to acquire comprehensive knowledge of significant biblical events, characters, and theological themes.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the Pentateuch by analysing the centrality of God and mankind, divine election and salvation, the significance of covenants, and the role of priests in order to guide spiritual, moral and ethical issues in modern times.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the creation accounts in Genesis 1 and 2 to understand the biblical perspective on the origin of man and the universe as desired by God. (u, v, s, gs)
demonstrate an appreciation for God’s creation by analysing the place of man in creation to develop a personal and intimate relationship with God through love and worship. (u, v/a, gs)
demonstrate appreciation for God by exploring His attributes as revealed through His works in the Pentateuch, and develop a deeper reverence for Him. (u, v, gs)
analyse the nature of man as presented in the Pentateuch by reading scriptures to recognise the uniqueness, purpose, and shortfalls of mankind. (u, v/a, gs)

analyse the theme of divine election and salvation as presented through key personalities and events in the Pentateuch, providing a foundation for evaluating modern ideas of deliverance from sin. (u, v/a, gs)

evaluate the concept of priesthood in Israel as described in Leviticus, examining the responsibilities and significance of priests in religious and social contexts, and reflecting on their influence on ancient Israelite society and their enduring impact on society today. (u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: Divine election and salvation (Genesis 12, 15, 17, 18, Exodus 16:1, 19:5-6, Deuteronomy 7:6-8, 8:3, 11-14, 9:4-6, 31:27, Leviticus 20:22-23)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners read the two creation stories in Genesis 1 and 2. In groups, learners identify and list the key differences and similarities between the two creation accounts. Learners debate on the different interpretations of the creation stories. Learners work in groups to discuss the creation stories. The groups make presentations in class under the guidance of the teacher. Learners brainstorm on the origin of mankind in Genesis 1 and 2. Learners discuss the place of man in the creation story. Learners write essays comparing the creation stories in the Pentateuch, discussing their cultural and religious significance.

In groups learners: read Genesis 1:1, Genesis 1:27, Genesis 17:1, Exodus 3:14, Exodus 20:2-3, Exodus 34:6-7, Deuteronomy 6:4-5, and Deuteronomy 7:9 to discover the nature of God. discuss the different attributes of God in the given scriptures. present their findings to the class and the teacher. individually, learners write a detailed description of God's attributes.

In pairs, learners read Genesis 1:26-28, 2:7, 3:1-24, 4:1-16, 5:12, 6:5, Exodus 19:5, Deuteronomy 8:11-14, Deuteronomy 9:4-6, Deuteronomy 31:27, Leviticus 20:22-23 to identify the purpose, uniqueness and shortfalls of man. In groups, learners discuss the identified themes based on given verses. Learners relate the discussed ideas in themes to the modern context. Learners make group presentations under the guidance of their teacher. Learners make write ups which include the verses on each of the following; uniqueness, purpose and shortfalls of mankind relating them to daily living.

In pairs, learners read Genesis 12, 15, 17, 18, Exodus 16:1, 19:5-6, Deuteronomy 7:6-8, 8:3 and 11-14, 9:4-6; 31:27, Leviticus 20:22-23. In groups, learners discuss the concept of divine election and its responsibilities. In pairs, learners discuss the significance and implications of being chosen by God. In groups, learners discuss the Abrahamic and Mosaic covenants, to establish their unique characteristics. In groups, learners compare the two covenants. Learners brainstorm the significance of God’s covenant/relationship with mankind. Learners make group presentations with the teacher’s guidance. Individually, learners write down their findings in notebooks.

In pairs, learners read Leviticus 8:1-36, 21:1-24. Learners discuss the ordination of Aaron and his sons. In groups, learners share insights on the roles and responsibilities of priests in the Old Testament. In pairs, learners identify and write the rules of conduct and purity for priests of the time. In groups, learners compare the rules of biblical times to those of the priests today. In groups, learners share their findings with the class under the guidance of the teacher. Individually, learners summarise the major ideas about priesthood in their notebooks.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Listen to the learners reading the appropriate Biblical texts noting their fluency. Listen to the learners debate and assess the accuracy and validity of their views in comprehending the creation stories. Observe the level of cooperation and respect of each other’s views during the debate and discussions. Assess the learners’ products for accuracy of the views presented focusing on the creation stories.

Listen to the quality of the discussion regarding the attributes of God from different Biblical texts and verses. Listen to the presentations by the learners focusing on articulation, relevance and accuracy of the facts. Assess the products in the form of a write-up focusing on the correctness of the facts and coherence.

Listen to the learners as they read, focusing on the accuracy of scriptures and fluency. Listen to the learners’ discussions and presentations focusing on the articulation, comprehension and accuracy of the issues presented. Listen to the learners discuss purpose, uniqueness and shortfalls of man. Assess the learners’ products for accuracy and coherence in presentation.

Observe the learners reading the given texts focusing on how they interact effectively with each other. Converse with the learners and task them to make simple explanations on the key personalities and events in the Pentateuch. Evaluate the learners’ comprehension of the biblical texts and their ability to collaborate and make individual contributions. Use a rubric to evaluate the essays based on criteria such as structure, use of examples, comparative analysis and quality of writing.

Evaluate their comprehension of the texts and ability to identify important themes. Assess each group's presentation of their insights on the roles and responsibilities of priests focusing on accuracy, clarity and presentation skills. Assess written assignments where learners identify and elaborate on the rules of conduct and purity for priests, focusing on completeness and accuracy.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses the Israelites' transition from migrant to settled life by focusing on the conquest, settlement and the role of judges in upholding the covenant faith and theocratic rule, in order to relate to the judicial roles in contemporary society.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Investigate Canaanite religion and the role of judges in ancient Israel, evaluating their impact on the moral, social, and political development of the Israelite community and its relevance to contemporary society. (u, s, v/a gs)

evaluate the priestly leadership of Eli and his family by using biblical scriptures to examine the consequences of their spiritual complacency and apply these insights to develop the value of accountability and discipline in church leadership today. (u, v, s, gs)
evaluate Samuel's leadership by examining his roles as a priest, prophet and judge to relate and guide modern leaders. (u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners analyse Joshua chapters 1-13 and 24 and Judges 1-12. Learners locate and discuss the role of judges in ancient Israel. In pairs, learners construct characteristics of Canaanite religion. In groups, learners discuss the rise of religious syncretism in Israel. In groups, learners dramatise the covenant renewal ceremony. Individually, learners write reflection essays on the significance of the ceremony.

In pairs, learners read 1 Samuel chapters 1 to 4. In groups, learners discuss the passages to identify key messages. In groups, learners relate the identified messages to contemporary society through discussion. The groups present their findings, focusing on accountability and discipline, and relate them to modern-day leadership of the church. Learners individually note the important issues in their books.

In groups, learners read the book of 1 Samuel chapters 1 to 25. In groups, learners identify and discuss Samuel's key actions, decisions, and qualities as a priest and judge. Learners relate Samuel’s role to those of the religious leaders today. In groups, learners present their insights, focusing on how Samuel's leadership principles can be applied to modern church roles. Individually, learners write an essay to compare Samuel’s leadership with modern church leaders, supported by specific examples from 1 Samuel and real-life church contexts.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe and listen to learners to assess understanding through their participation and insights as they read and discuss noting how confidently they present their ideas. Converse with the learners as they work effectively in diverse teams noting accuracy and completeness. Watch, listen, and assess the learners focusing on their understanding of the covenant renewal ceremony, checking their creativity and performance skills. Assess the written product focusing on accuracy and coherence of the facts presented in the essays.

Observe the learners’ conduct in the groups focusing on how they interact effectively with others. Listen to the discussions focusing on fluency and accuracy on the priestly leadership of Eli and his family. Assess the product by looking out for accuracy and coherence of the ideas presented about leadership in Israel and churches today.

Monitor participation and engagement during reading sessions to ascertain how the learners take responsibility for their learning. Observe and note contributions to the discussion as well as the learners’ time management. Observe and assess participation and understanding focusing on sorting and analysing information. Assess essays based on a rubric with criteria such as depth of analysis, use of evidence, clarity of arguments, and relevance to modern contexts.

topics.core_competency: The learner develops an understanding of monarchism in ancient Israel by analysing the establishment, leadership, and impact of key monarchs, and assessing the socio-political, religious, and cultural implications for ancient Israelite society, and relates it to modern governance and leadership.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the demand for human kingship in Israel by exploring the societal, political, and religious factors that drove this shift from theocratic leadership, and evaluating its impact on Israelite governance and identity. (u, v, s, gs)

analyse the leadership styles and governance of human kings in Israel by exploring the political, social, and religious impact of their rule on the development and identity of ancient Israelite society and lessons learnt from their leadership. (u, v/a, gs)

analyse the division of the kingdom of Israel by examining biblical scriptures to assess the roles of key figures and consequences, in order to appreciate God's power, sovereignty, and the importance of leadership accountability in modern society. (u, v/a, s, gs)

evaluate the reforms enacted by kings in Israel, examining the social, political, and religious changes they implemented, and assessing their impact on the development and preservation of Israelite society. (u, v/a, s, gs)

must_cover: Leadership of Saul, David, and Solomon (1 and 2 Samuel, 1 Kings)
Division of the kingdom (2 Samuel, 1 Kings)
Reforms by kings (2 Kings, Josiah, Hezekiah)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners debate the motion "Theocracy vs. Monarchy" to express the pros and cons of each leadership model. Learners engage in a Socratic seminar to discuss key questions about the shift from theocracy to monarchy and its implications. In groups, learners read 1 Samuel 8: 1-21. In groups, learners discuss the social, political, and religious reasons for the Israelite demand for a king. In groups, learners present their findings, focusing on different aspects such as societal unrest, political instability, and religious implications. In groups, learners discuss God’s warnings through Samuel about kingship. Learners make presentations about factors for the rise of kingship and God’s warnings on human kingship. Individually, Learners write an essay about human kingship in Israel and the fears that surrounded it.

In groups: learners analyse 1 and 2 Samuel and 1 Kings to identify how Kings Saul, David and Solomon rose to power. learners discuss the achievements and failures of Kings Saul, David and Solomon. learners discuss and relate the leadership styles of political leaders today. learners present their findings to the class and the teacher. Individually, learners write down the major ideas on kingship.

In groups, learners read 2 Samuel and 1 Kings to discuss the background to the division of the kingdom. Learner identify key players in the division of the kingdom. Learners summarise the impact of the division of the kingdom to the people and religion. In groups, learners relate the aspect of the division of the kingdom of Israel to divisionism in modern society. In groups, learners share their findings with the class using visual aids. Individually, learners write essays relating the division of the kingdom of Israel to divisions in contemporary society.

In groups, learners read 2 Kings to discover the reformist kings of Judah and their significance. In pairs, learners discuss the situation before the reforms. In pairs, learners identify the reforms made by kings Josiah and Hezekiah. In groups, learners relate the reforms to areas that need reforms today. In groups, the learners make presentations to the rest of the class and teacher. Individually, learners summarise the key ideas in their notebooks.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe participation and engagement during the debate focusing on the learners’ levels of critical thinking, public speaking skills and respect for one another. Listen to learners during presentations, focusing on the ability to ask and respond to thought-provoking questions. Observe the learners and look out for group participation and collaborative reading. Listen to and assess the quality of discussions, including relevance, depth of analysis, and use of examples. Assess the learners’ ability to interpret and discuss biblical warnings about human kingship. Listen to the learners’ discussions to assess the ability to derive lessons from God’s warnings to Christians today. Use an essay rubric to assess structure, argument, evidence, and writing quality.

Observe learners as they read and look out for group participation and collaborative reading and comprehension. Converse with learners, paying attention to the quality of discussions on the rise to power, achievements and failures of Israelite kings. Listen to the discussions as learners relate the leadership styles focusing on levels of analysis and quality of arguments. Assess the written ideas presented by the learners focusing on accuracy and coherence within the presentation.

Listen to the learners’ responses to questions about key players and events to assess their understanding. Observe learners to assess their engagement and contributions during discussions, focusing on the relevance and depth of their insights. Listen to learners to analyse their understanding of the historical and political context and their ability to articulate these ideas. Read learners’ products to evaluate the ability to analyse and summarise the consequences of the division on society and religion. Read the learners’ essays to relate the historical division to modern examples of political or religious divisions. Listen to the learners as they draw parallels between ancient division and contemporary events.

Listen to learners read 2 Kings to assess their comprehension. Listen to the discussions to assess the quality and accuracy of the presentations. Read the learners’ products to assess their accuracy and coherence. Evaluate the learners’ discussions and products as they compare the reforms of the time with those of today.

topics.core_competency: Learners appreciate the significance of prophetic work in ancient Israel, by examining the social, political, and economic contexts of the time, exploring the theme of the broken covenant, and analysing the general messages delivered by the selected prophets in order to build a contemporary understanding of justice, leadership, and community values.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the social, political, and economic contexts of the prophets' time, assessing their relevance and connections to contemporary issues. (u, v/a, gs)

analyse the themes of the broken covenant, call for repentance, judgement and the day of the Lord, hope and individual responsibility, as addressed by selected prophets, relating their messages to contemporary social, ethical, and spiritual issues. (u, s, v, gs)

synthesise the core messages of Old Testament prophets by analysing their books, identifying major themes, and exploring their relevance, to inform responses to modern ethical, social, and spiritual issues. (u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: Prophetic books of Amos, Isaiah, and Ezekiel

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use ICT to study the selected prophetic books of Amos, Isaiah, and Ezekiel. In groups, learners search for verses that address the social, political, and economic evils of their time. In pairs, learners relate their findings to modern-day evils. In pairs, learners suggest solutions to address contemporary social religious, economic and political injustices. In groups, learners present to the rest of the class and teacher. Individually, learners write an essay on the key ideas in their notebooks.

In groups, learners read the books of Amos and Isaiah to search for evidence of the broken covenant. learners discuss the song of the vine yard (Isaiah 5) to portray the broken covenant. learners present their ideas to the class. Learners discuss and share how people today have broken their covenant with God, and suggest ways in which Christians can restore their relationships with God. Individually, learners summarise the key ideas in their notebooks.

In groups, learners read and analyse the prophetic books to identify the following selected themes: Judgement: a. Isaiah 1, 2, 5, 13 and 24; b. Amos 1, 3, 5, 6, 7 and so on. Hope: a. Isaiah 9 and 11; b. Isaiah 40. Day of the Lord: a. Isaiah 2 and Amos 5. Individual responsibility for sin: b. Ezekiel 18, 33:10-20. Learners discuss and share the main ideas with the class using charts and mind maps. individually, learners summarise the key ideas in their notebooks.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Assess the learners’ digital portfolio where they tabulate prophetic ideas, using spreadsheets or databases focusing on accuracy, organisation, and completeness of the classifications. Listen to learners as they read to establish their comprehension of prophetic messages. Facilitate and observe learner discussions to assess the depth, accuracy, and relevance of their conversations. Listen to the learners as they relate what happened then to modern times. Read the learners’ products focusing on the logical coherence, depth of analysis, and relevance of their conclusions.

Listen to and converse with learners as they read and interpret biblical texts focusing on their ability to explain their ideas clearly to establish comprehension. Observe to evaluate the learners’ creativity and the accuracy of their ideas as they make presentations. Assess the products presented by learners focusing on the accuracy and coherence of the facts presented.

Observe learners as they locate verses on judgment, hope, the Day of the Lord and individual responsibility focusing on their effective interaction with others. Converse with learners as they discuss the texts on judgement, hope, the Day of the Lord, and individual responsibility. Assess the learners’ charts or mind maps identifying different themes in the prophetic books focusing on accuracy, completeness, and organisation skills. Listen intentionally to the learners’ presentations to evaluate their ability to recognize and categorize themes in the prophetic texts. Use a participation rubric to evaluate engagement and contributions during their discussion. Listen to the learners’ discussion focusing on comprehension of the prophetic messages of judgment and ability to analyse biblical texts.

suggested_uses: Use ICT to study the selected prophetic books of Amos, Isaiah, and Ezekiel
Use digital portfolio for tabulating prophetic ideas

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates appreciation of perseverance and worship in ancient Israel through applying the teachings of Job and Psalms; analysing the themes of suffering, faith, and divine justice in Job; and exploring the expressions of worship, lament, and thanksgiving in Psalms to enable people in the modern society connect these ancient insights to contemporary issues.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the themes of suffering, justice, and patience in the book of Job, relating them to contemporary challenges to explore resilience and meaning in adversity. (u, v/a, s, gs)
evaluate the significance of dialogue and reflection in the Book of Job, applying these insights to modern discussions about empathy, support, and understanding during crises. (u, v/a, gs)
appreciate the emotional and spiritual expressions in Psalms 2, 20, 22, 47, and 147, and reflect on how these texts shape contemporary worship practices and personal devotional life. (u, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners read the book of Job. In groups, learners discuss the theme of suffering as indicated in the Book of Job. In pairs, learners trace the theme of justice in the book of Job. Learners brainstorm the aspects of patience in the book of Job. In groups, learners relate the themes to modern day challenges and suggest ways of overcoming them.

In groups, learners dramatise the dialogue between Job and his wife; and Job and his friends. In pairs, learners discuss the relevance of the dialogues to modern Christians. Individually, learners write down the important messages from the drama guided by the themes.

In groups, learners use ICT and other resources to discover the rationale of using Psalms in ancient Israel. In pairs, learners read all the Psalms to identify and discuss the emotional and spiritual expressions in them. In pairs, discuss the message in each of the Psalms. In pairs, relate each Psalm to daily worship practices today. In groups, learners share their findings with the rest of the class with the teacher’s guidance. Individually, learners summarise and tabulate the emotional and spiritual expressions in each Psalm.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Listen to learners read and comment on the message of Job focusing on the accuracy of the comments and discussions. Listen to learners’ discussions on the key events and characters in the book of Job to assess their understanding. Assess the learners’ essays where they relate the themes of suffering, justice, and patience in the book of Job to modern day challenges and discuss strategies for overcoming them.

Observe the learners’ drama to evaluate them basing on criteria such as accuracy, expression, collaboration, and adherence to the text. Observe the learners to evaluate their participation in the discussion, considering the relevance, depth of insights, and ability to connect the dialogue to contemporary Christian living. Read the learners’ written summaries on the important messages conveyed in the drama focusing on comprehensiveness, clarity, and accuracy.

Converse with the learners as they read and discuss, focusing on accuracy and relevancy of the discussion. Read the products presented for accuracy. Listen to the presentations focusing on their relevance and accuracy.

suggested_uses: Use ICT to discover the rationale of using Psalms in ancient Israel

topics.core_competency: The learner examines the historical, cultural, and religious context of the apostolic period, by evaluating the New Testament canonisation process, and reflecting on its significance and influence on modern Christian practice.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: investigate the link between the Old and New Testaments, focusing on the theme of Messiahship, to understand how the Old Testament foreshadows and lays the groundwork for the New Testament. (u, v/a, gs)

explore the features of the early church by analysing the message of the original gospel and early worship practices to gain insight into the birth of Christianity and how it shapes modern Christian practices. (u, v/a, gs)

assess the origin, development, and criteria underlying the compilation of the New Testament Canon, recognising its divine inspiration to deepen reverence of the New Testament as the inspired Word of God that is relevant to the contemporary church. (u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners read and analyse Genesis chapters 1 to 3, 12:1-3, Exodus 20:1-17, Leviticus 8:1-36, 16:1-36, Deuteronomy 27:26, 2 Samuel 7:12-13, Daniel 12:2-3, Isaiah 53:1-12, Zechariah 9:9, Mark 11, Luke 1:32-33, John1:1, 3:16, 11:25-26, 12:15, Romans 6:14-15, Galatians 3:6-9, 11, Hebrews 5:1-10, 9:11-14, Learners discuss the interconnection between the Old and New Testaments with reference to the above Biblical texts. In groups, learners derive the relevance of the above texts to Christians today. In groups, learners present their findings to the rest of the class with the teacher’s guidance. Individually, learners summarise the similarities and differences between the Old and New Testaments in their notebooks.

In groups, learners: use the internet, Bible, and any other resources to search the contents of the Kerygma, its advantages and demerits as well as the general features of the early Church. analyse the oral method of preaching the Gospel. discuss the main activities of the early Church citing their relevance for the contemporary churches. share findings with the rest of the class in a presentation. Individually, learners write the major points.

In groups, learners: brainstorm the reasons for writing the New Testament canon. justify the selection of the New Testament canon. analyse the process of forming the New Testament canon. examine the criteria used to select the 27 books. Discuss the relevance of the selected books to Christians today. present ideas to the rest of the class. Individually, learners summarise the major points in their notebooks.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they read the Bible texts and look out for group participation and collaborative reading and comprehension. Converse with the learners to evaluate the quality and accuracy of the discussed ideas. Assess the product in form of a table checking for accuracy of tabulated ideas. Read the products to evaluate accuracy and relevance.

Converse with learners as they carry out research. Observe each individual learner’s contribution to the discussion. Converse with the learners to ascertain their understanding of the period of oral gospel. Check each learner’s notebook for accuracy.

Observe learners as they discuss to ascertain the correctness and authenticity of their ideas and look out for group participation and collaborative reading and comprehension. Converse with the learners to gauge each individual learner’s contribution to the discussion. Check each learner’s exercise books to assess the accuracy of the summarised ideas.

suggested_uses: use the internet, Bible, and any other resources to search the contents of the Kerygma

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates an understanding of the selected themes and perspectives in the Gospels of John and Mark, recognising their unique contributions to the development of Christian faith, and applies them to address contemporary issues.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: analyse the preaching of John the Baptist as depicted in the Gospels of Mark and John, assessing his messages of repentance and preparing the way for Jesus, and reflecting on the relevance of these teachings to modern Christians. (u, v/a, s, gs)

examine the different methods used by Jesus to convey his message about the kingdom of God in John and Mark through analysing parables and discourses drawing their relevance to Christians today. (u, v/a, gs)

evaluate the significance of miracles in the Gospel of Mark and signs in John by analysing their implications and exploring how these events can inspire faith and hope in the contemporary world. (u, v/a, s, gs)

analyse the instances of acceptance, controversies, and opposition that Jesus encountered in the Gospel according to Mark drawing the relevance of unwavering faith and commitment in the contemporary world. (u, v/a, s, gs)

analyse the passion, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ by examining the biblical texts in Mark reflecting on how these events can inspire resilience, empathy and compassion in their own lives and communities. (u, v/a, s, gs)

must_cover: Preaching of John the Baptist (Mark 1:1-8, John 1:19-28)
Passion, death, and resurrection in Mark (Mark 14, 15, 16)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners: read the scriptures about the preaching of John the Baptist in the gospels according to Mark 1:1-8 and John 1:19-28. discuss the key messages in the preaching of John the Baptist. discuss the relevance of John the Baptist to Christians today. present the discussed ideas to the rest of the class and teacher. Individually, learners summarise the main points in their notebooks.

In groups, learners: read Mark 4: 1-20 and 12:1-12 and discuss the message and meanings of the parables. read John 3:1-21, 4:1-42, 8:1-11 and derive the message of Jesus’ teaching in the discourses. discuss the relevance of Jesus’ parables and discourses to Christians today. make presentations to the class and the teacher. individually write the main ideas in their notebooks.

In groups, learners: analyse the Biblical texts provided; Mark 2:1-12, 5:1-20, John 2:1-12, 11:1-44. discuss the messages of the selected miracles in Mark and signs in John and their relevance to Christians today. evaluate and form opinions about miracles in the contemporary world. present and share ideas with the rest of the class. Individually, learners write down summarised notes on the key ideas about the manifestation of God’s kingdom in Mark and John.

In groups, learners: read the Gospel according to Mark tracing the reactions of various categories of people to Jesus Christ’s public ministry (that is, the Pharisees, Scribes, Sadducees, Priests and teachers of the law, women, Gentiles, the twelve disciples and the people of Nazareth). explain the reasons why Jesus faced opposition and rejection in His public ministry. investigate Jesus’ reaction in the face of opposition. identify instances when Christians face opposition today. explain the lessons Christians can draw from people's responses and Jesus’ reaction to opposition and rejection. present and share the discussed ideas with the rest of the class. Individually, learners summarise the key points in their notebooks.

In groups: learners analyse Mark 14, 15, and 16. learners use ICT to watch a movie on the passion of Jesus or role-play the arrest, death, and resurrection of Jesus according to the gospel of Mark. learners discuss the significance of the key events in the passion narratives in the gospel according to Mark namely the, the anointment of Jesus; the Lord’s Supper, prayer in Gethsemane, death and the resurrection. learners examine the relevance of Jesus’ passion to modern Christians following the selected events. learners present their findings to their classmates and the teacher. Individually, learners summarise the main ideas in their notebooks.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they read, discuss and compare John the Baptist’s message and ministry in the gospels according to Mark and John focusing on fluency, accuracy and individual participation. Converse with learners as they interpret and draw the relevance of John the Baptist’s teachings to Christians today. Check each learner’s exercise books to assess the accuracy and coherence of the ideas noted down about the ministry of John the Baptist.

Observe and listen to learners as they read and discuss to ensure they interpret and comprehend the message of parables in Mark. Converse with the learners and probe them as they read and discuss the message of the selected discourses in John focusing on the insights to modern Christians. Assess the accuracy of the learners’ ideas regarding the meaning of the selected parables and discourses in the gospels to ensure proper interpretation. check for the quality and accuracy of the write-up focusing on individuals working independently.

Observe learners as they read and discuss the divine messages of the selected miracles and signs in Mark and John focusing on teamwork, comprehension, ability to draw lessons and correct interpretation of the biblical texts. Converse with the learners as they form opinions and draw lessons and relevance from the selected miracles and signs in Mark and John laying emphasis on active individual participation. Assess the accuracy of the learners’ ideas in regard to the selected miracles and signs focusing on the logical flow of ideas. Check the learners’ books to assess the accuracy of the written summaries.

Observe the learners as they read and brainstorm the reactions of the audience to Jesus’ ministry focusing on their ability to explain the key points of Jesus’ response to people’s reactions. Converse with the learners as they draw out the lessons and relevance of the reactions of different categories of people to Jesus’ ministry. Check learner’s exercise books to assess the accuracy and logical flow of ideas of the summarised write-ups.

Observe learners as they read to inspire them to listen and comprehend the selected biblical texts. Converse with the learners as they dramatise or watch a movie about the passion, death and resurrection of Jesus focusing on the creativity and individual participation. Listen to the learners’ ideas as they draw lessons from Bible texts focusing on critical thinking and generate positive insights. Check the learners’ note books to ensure accuracy and coherence of the written ideas.

suggested_uses: use ICT to watch a movie on the passion of Jesus
